title: Affine-line compact-support adjunction for all certified adic rings
statement: Fix a universe u, a prime ell and a field k of positive characteristic different from ell. All schemes are separated finite-type k-schemes in u. Let Lambda be a commutative condensed ring with a certificate IsEllAdicCoefficient ell Lambda, allowing continuous finite extensions, integral valuation rings with torsion, and the finite-subextension-valued algebraic closure [def-sfb-adic-coefficient-certificate]. Write B_T for the full bounded constructible subcategory of the ordinary unbounded derived category of internal Lambda_T-module objects [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible; sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. For each standing scheme T put A=A^1_T with its one-element coordinate type PUnit, and let p:A -> T be the projection. The actual compactification-based functor boundedConstructibleLowerShriek Lambda ell p:B_A -> B_T has a right adjoint, expressed by Functor.IsLeftAdjoint. The redundant IsFinitenessCoefficient hypothesis is deduced from the coefficient certificate. No completeness, finite Tor-amplitude or torsion-free hypothesis is added; integral torsion is permitted.

proof.text: On P1_T construct eta_M from the diagonal class Delta_*R -> R(1)[2], proper base change and the projection formula. Construct epsilon_K by projection formula and the projective-line trace. Rewriting the two triangle composites gives respectively 1 tensor tr_r1(Rr1_*delta) and 1 tensor tr_r2(Rr2_*delta). Both are identities by trace/diagonal normalization. Naturality then makes h -> G(h)eta and a -> epsilon F(a) inverse Hom maps. The integral calculation permits torsion. The rational cases use the compatible finite-field and finite-subextension-valued traces.

Compose the projective-line adjunction with the exact standard affine-chart adjunction Dj! left adjoint to Dj*. Pullback composition and Cartesian Tate lines identify the right-hand functor with p*(-)(1)[2]. Compare the chart compactification with the chosen compactification by the coefficient-uniform comparison proved in the compact-support composition module.

Pullback is exact and preserves constructibility. The Tate line is locally free of rank one, so tensoring is an exact equivalence; on each stratum refine by a line-trivializing cover to preserve the finitely presented model. Shifts reindex a finite homology range. Thus both adjoint functors preserve bounded constructibility, and their ambient Hom equivalences restrict to a bounded constructible adjunction. No derived completion is used.

theorem affineLine_compactSupport_isLeftAdjoint
    (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType T.hom] [QuasiCompact T.hom] [IsSeparated T.hom] :
    let A : Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
      Over.mk ((𝔸(PUnit.{u + 1}; T.left) ↘ T.left) ≫ T.hom)
    let p : A ⟶ T := Over.homMk (𝔸(PUnit.{u + 1}; T.left) ↘ T.left) rfl
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType A.hom :=
      inferInstanceAs (LocallyOfFiniteType ((𝔸(PUnit.{u + 1}; T.left) ↘ T.left) ≫ T.hom))
    letI : QuasiCompact A.hom :=
      inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact ((𝔸(PUnit.{u + 1}; T.left) ↘ T.left) ≫ T.hom))
    letI : IsSeparated A.hom :=
      inferInstanceAs (IsSeparated ((𝔸(PUnit.{u + 1}; T.left) ↘ T.left) ≫ T.hom))
    (boundedConstructibleLowerShriek Λ ℓ p).IsLeftAdjoint
